docs.title: 📐 TriggerForge Architecture Specification
docs.text: Version: v1.1-PRO Status: Approved Scope: System core blueprint and isolation model specification, serving as the definitive guide for core engineering and development.

docs.title: I. System Architecture Overview
docs.text:
TriggerForge implements a strictly decoupled four-layer isolation architecture model. This design guarantees absolute stability and self-healing capabilities for the core engine, even under heavy concurrent file events, untrusted third-party plugin crashes, or severe memory leaks.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 Looper (Main Loop / Orchestrator)               │
│   load config → per folder: Watcher + Queue + Worker Threads     │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Sentry (Sentinel Watcher Layer)                │
│   Watchdog events → temp filter → debounce Timer → enqueue       │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                               │  EventBufferQueue (thread-safe)
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  ForgeCore (Execution Engine Layer)              │
│   workers consume queue → sequential strategies → subprocess     │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Clerk (Output Manager Layer)                  │
│   success → success_path / failure → error_path + .panic.json    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 1. Looper (Main Loop Layer)
docs.text:
• Responsibilities: Serves as the outermost long-running daemon process of the system. It handles the entire lifecycle of the TriggerForge engine, including initialization, configuration loading, graceful shutdown sequencing, and global OS signal handling.
  • Orchestration: For every watched directory it instantiates a SentryWatcher plus an EventBufferQueue, then spawns concurrency worker threads that consume the queue and drive the full "run plugins → archive" pipeline.
  • Self-Healing Mechanics: Ensures zero configuration loss during catastrophic unexpected global errors, maintaining the capacity to dynamically reboot downstream layers.

docs.title: 2. Sentry (Sentinel Watcher Layer)
docs.text:
• Responsibilities: Filesystem event ingestion, static filtering, and write debouncing.
  • Technical Implementation:
  • Watchdog Poller: Listens for real-time filesystem events (on_created / on_modified) on the configured directories.
  • Static Filtering: Drops temp/editor artifacts (.tmp, .swp, trailing ~, dotfiles) before they reach the pipeline.
  • Write Debouncing: A per-path Timer is cancelled and rescheduled for repeated events inside the debounce_seconds window, guaranteeing downstream plugins only see fully written files.
  • Buffered Handoff: Once the debounce window expires, the path is enqueued into the thread-safe EventBufferQueue, decoupling ingestion from execution and absorbing bursts.

docs.title: 3. ForgeCore (Execution Engine Layer)
docs.text:
• Responsibilities: Host environment and execution pipeline coordinator for plugins.
  • Execution Flow: worker threads pull a path from EventBufferQueue and run strategies sequentially; the first failure short-circuits the remaining strategies.
  • Subprocess Sandbox Isolation:
  • Hard Process Isolation: ForgeCore strictly prohibits executing third-party plugin code within the main process or worker threads. For every strategy it spawns a completely independent subprocess via PluginRunner, invoked as main.py <file_path> <json_params>.
  • Fault and Crash Isolation: Plugin child processes possess their own isolated memory space and are bounded by hard execution timeout fences. If a plugin suffers a memory leak, enters an infinite loop, or encounters a sudden segmentation fault (Segfault), only that specific subprocess is impacted. ForgeCore safely destroys the corrupted child process, reclaims system resources, and leaves the core engine 100% unaffected.
  • Multi-Version Virtual Environment Support: Supports explicitly defining a custom python_path in the configuration. This allows child processes to dynamically invoke separate, fully-isolated Python virtual environments (Venvs), seamlessly solving dependency conflicts between legacy and modern plugins. Invalid paths fall back to the current interpreter with a warning.

docs.title: 4. Clerk (Output Manager Layer)
docs.text:
• Responsibilities: Manages the post-execution cleanup, file lifecycle tracking, and state materialization.
  • Asset & Diagnostics Routing:
  • Pipeline Archiving: Automatically moves processed files to either success_path (Success Archive) or error_path (Error Archive) based on the exact status returned by the plugin subprocess, with directory self-healing and timestamp-based collision avoidance.
  • Panic Dumps: When a plugin fails, times out, or crashes, Clerk writes a structured panic_{plugin}_{timestamp}.json containing target file metadata, the failing plugin and strategy params, environment context, and the captured stdout / stderr streams — providing immediate, zero-consultation troubleshooting evidence for SRE teams.

docs.title: 1. Architecture as Code
docs.text:
Static documentation inevitably degrades and drifts as code iterates. TriggerForge declares all system metadata (such as watch_folders, concurrency, strategies, etc.) programmatically via Python Type Hints + Pydantic Schemas inside src/triggerforge/core/schema.py, which is the single source of truth for configuration fields.

The companion docs/zh/configuration.md and docs/en/configuration.md must stay in sync with the schema: update the field tables whenever a field is added or changed. The guard test tests/unit/test_schema.py::test_repo_sample_config_is_valid additionally ensures config.yaml and config.sample.yaml always validate against the schema, preventing config/implementation drift.

docs.title: 2. Modern Python Source Layout (src/ Layout)
docs.text: The project abandons traditional nested module architectures in favor of the clean, modern src/ layout backed by the Hatch build system. The core source code resides under src/triggerforge/. This eliminates the risk of implicit local path contamination within PYTHONPATH during testing and development, guaranteeing a pure and predictable build distribution when packaged into a Wheel file.

docs.title: 3. Deterministic CI/CD and Flaky Test Elimination
docs.text: To guarantee that CI/CD pipelines remain 100% stable in containerized or virtualized environments (such as GitHub Actions), integration tests inside the tests/ directory are completely decoupled from OS-level disk I/O hooks. The test suite leverages an in-memory mock queue filesystem declared via tests/conftest.py. This mock event system fires deterministic event streams in memory, completely eliminating intermittent test suite timeouts caused by OS file event processing latencies.

docs.title: 📜 TriggerForge Project Charter
docs.text: Version: v1.1-PRO Status: Approved Scope: Defines the core business pain points, system boundaries, and technical vision of TriggerForge, serving as the foundational governance document for project initialization.

docs.title: I. Core Pain Points & Project Background
docs.text:
In modern enterprise automation pipelines and data processing workflows, triggering downstream business logic (such as file decompression, format conversion, and data parsing) by watching filesystem directory events is a ubiquitous requirement. However, conventional scripts and lightweight utilities frequently suffer from three fatal pain points in production environments:

  1. "Zombie Documentation" and Configuration Drift: Traditional system configurations are completely disconnected from developer documentation. As the project iterates rapidly, static markdown files quickly become outdated, eventually turning into misleading trash that confuses onboarding engineers.
  2. "Single Point of Failure" in Plugin Environments: Third-party plugins or legacy scripts are often poorly written. When a plugin encounters a memory leak, enters an infinite loop, or triggers a sudden segmentation fault (Segfault), it typically crashes the entire main monitoring process due to a complete lack of fault isolation boundaries.
  3. Flaky Tests Polluting CI/CD Pipelines: Because underlying libraries like Watchdog rely heavily on native OS filesystem hooks, they often exhibit extreme instability—manifested as intermittent test timeouts—in containerized or virtualized CI/CD environments (such as GitHub Actions) due to disk I/O latencies. This consumes massive maintenance effort from the engineering team.

TriggerForge is engineered to systematically eliminate these engineering dysfunctions. It rejects the "good enough to run" mindset of temporary scripts, establishing itself as a full-lifecycle engineering product featuring enterprise-grade process isolation, automated document generation, and production-ready deployment solutions.

docs.title: II. Technical Vision & Strategic Goals
docs.text: The core vision of TriggerForge is to build a modern, event-driven directory orchestration engine that is resilient under pressure, completely fault-isolated, self-documenting, highly collaborative, and open-source compliant.

docs.title: 1. Core Engineering Targets
docs.text:
• Architecture as Code: Leverage the Python type system and Pydantic schemas as the definitive source of truth for "living documentation." Manual editing of configuration specifications is strictly prohibited; all field metadata is auto-generated from the system schema to eradicate document drift.
  • Hardcore Subprocess Sandbox Isolation: Spawn an independent child process for every plugin execution, bounded by strict execution timeout fences and resource perimeters. This guarantees that runtime failures are perfectly locked inside the sub-environment.
  • Cloud-Native & CI/CD Determinism: Introduce an in-memory mock queue filesystem to bypass native disk I/O within containerized environments, ensuring that testing pipelines pass with 100% stability and consistency.

docs.title: 1. In-Scope Deliverables
docs.text:
• Modern Source Layout: Implements a clean src/ layout matching the modern Python community's best practices, managed via a standard pyproject.toml configuration utilizing the Hatch build backend and PEP 621 specifications.
  • Non-Blocking Concurrent Event Dispatching: A decoupled workflow where the main loop (Looper) and the sentinel watcher (Sentry) communicate through a thread-safe buffer queue (EventBufferQueue) consumed by a pool of worker threads sized by concurrency, ensuring the main ingestion stream is never blocked.
  • Dynamic Multi-Venv Environments: Supports explicitly specifying a custom python_path inside the configuration, allowing child processes to dynamically invoke separate, fully-isolated virtual environments to seamlessly execute legacy plugins.
  • Production-Grade Operations Lifecycle: Provides an out-of-the-box Linux Systemd configuration for process守护 (daemonization), paired with journald-based log stream observability and automated structured .panic.json diagnostic reports (including full stdout/stderr) for post-mortem analysis.

docs.title: 2. Out-of-Scope Boundaries
docs.text: • Network API Endpoints: The v1.1-PRO release is strictly scoped as a resident local background daemon. It does not adapt to, nor does it provide, any HTTP/RESTful network interfaces, preserving complete architectural simplicity and core focus.

docs.title: IV. Commercial & Open-Source Roadmap
docs.text:
To balance the ecosystem benefits of open-source community collaboration with the commercial value of enterprise close-loop deployments, TriggerForge adopts a Dual-Licensing Model:

  1. Open-Source Version (GNU GPL v3): Targeted at personal use, academic research, and open-source community development. The source code is entirely transparent and protected by the copyleft nature of the GPL v3 license—any derivative works or integrated products distributed externally must also publish their full source code.
  2. Commercial License: Targeted at enterprise customers wishing to integrate TriggerForge into proprietary commercial software or SaaS platforms without being bound by GPL copyleft restrictions. This tier provides closed-source integration rights, custom plugin engineering, and SRE-grade enterprise support agreements.
  3. Contributor Compliance: Every external developer submitting a Pull Request to this repository must sign a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) to protect the integrity of the project's copyright ownership and ensure the legal distribution of the commercial edition.

docs.title: ⚙️ TriggerForge Configuration Specification
docs.text: Version: v1.1-PRO Source of truth: src/triggerforge/core/schema.py Notice: Field definitions on this page mirror the Pydantic models in schema.py. Keep them in sync when the schema changes.

docs.title: I. Global Configuration Parameters
docs.text: The TriggerForge main configuration file uses the standard YAML format. Core parameters are split into two modules: Global Dispatching Parameters and Directory Monitoring Strategies.

docs.title: 1. Core Field Definition
docs.text: Field Name Type Default Status Description watch_folders List[WatchFolderSchema] none (Required) List of monitored directory strategies. Multiple independent directories are supported. plugin_directory str "./plugins" Optional Plugin root directory. The engine resolves {plugin_name}/main.py inside it. debounce_seconds float 1.0 Optional Global default write-debounce window (seconds), must be > 0. Overridable per watch folder.

docs.title: 2. WatchFolderSchema (Directory Monitor Configuration Object)
docs.text: Field Name Type Default Status Description path str none (Required) Directory to watch. Dropping a file here triggers the plugin pipeline. success_path str none (Required) Archive directory for files whose full pipeline succeeded (atomic move). error_path str none (Required) Quarantine directory for files that failed or timed out (atomic move). concurrency int 1 Optional Number of worker threads assigned to this directory, must be > 0. debounce_seconds float 1.0 Optional Directory-specific write-debounce window (seconds), must be > 0. strategies List[StrategySchema] none (Required) Ordered, sequentially executed plugin strategy pipeline.

docs.title: 3. StrategySchema (Plugin Execution Strategy Configuration Object)
docs.text: Field Name Type Default Status Description plugin_name str none (Required) Plugin directory name; resolves {plugin_directory}/{plugin_name}/main.py. plugin_version str "0.0.0" Optional Plugin version marker used for runtime validation and auditing. timeout int 30 Optional Hard timeout (seconds) for the plugin subprocess, must be > 0. params Dict[str, Any] {} Optional Dynamic custom parameters injected into the plugin subprocess as JSON. python_path Optional[str] None Optional Path to an isolated interpreter (virtualenv). Falls back to the current interpreter if missing.

docs.title: II. Production-Ready Configuration Sample (config.sample.yaml)
docs.text:
Below is a production-grade configuration sample. Copy it to create your local config.yaml:

# =================================================================
# TriggerForge Production Configuration Blueprint
# =================================================================

# Plugin root: the engine resolves {plugin_directory}/{plugin_name}/main.py
plugin_directory: "./plugins"

# Global default debounce window (seconds); overridable per watch folder
debounce_seconds: 1.0

watch_folders:
  - path: "./storage/watch_folder"        # dropping a file here triggers the pipeline
    success_path: "./storage/success_folder"
    error_path: "./storage/error_folder"
    concurrency: 4                        # dedicated worker threads for this directory
    debounce_seconds: 1.0                 # directory-specific debounce window

    strategies:
      # Strategy 1: modern compression plugin with a 15s hard timeout
      - plugin_name: "compress_plugin"
        plugin_version: "1.0.0"
        timeout: 15
        params:
          level: "high"
          archive_type: "tar.gz"

      # Strategy 2: legacy parser running inside an isolated virtualenv
      - plugin_name: "legacy_parser_plugin"
        plugin_version: "0.8.2"
        python_path: "/opt/venv/legacy_env/bin/python"
        timeout: 30
        params:
          legacy_mode: true
          encoding: "gbk"

docs.title: III. Runtime Behavior
docs.text:
1. Event path: file written into the watched directory → debounce window waits for the write to finish → event enters the buffer queue → worker thread consumes it → strategies run sequentially.
  2. Short-circuit: if any strategy fails, remaining strategies are skipped and the file goes to the error zone.
  3. Archiving: all strategies succeeded → success_path; any failure → a .panic.json diagnostic report is written and the file is moved to error_path.
  4. Validation: config is validated at startup via TriggerForgeConfigSchema; use --dry-run to validate without starting watchers.

# ⚙️ TriggerForge Production Deployment & Operations Guide

> **Version**: v1.1-PRO  
> **Status**: Approved  
> **Scope**: Production daemon deployment and containerized orchestration blueprint for SREs, DevOps engineers, and system administrators.

---

## I. Daemon Management via Systemd (Recommended for Linux)

As a resident event-driven engine, TriggerForge must be managed by the Systemd service manager in production environments to guarantee autostart on boot and crash self-healing capabilities.

### 1. Creating the Service Configuration
Create a service definition file at `/etc/systemd/system/triggerforge.service` and populate it with the following configuration:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=TriggerForge Event-Driven Directory Orchestration Engine
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=triggerforge
Group=triggerforge
WorkingDirectory=/opt/triggerforge

# Critical Detail: Inject the correct global PYTHONPATH to match the modern src/ layout
Environment=PYTHONPATH=/opt/triggerforge/src

# Invoke the Python interpreter inside the Venv to boot up the core main module directly
ExecStart=/opt/triggerforge/venv/bin/python -m triggerforge.main --config /opt/triggerforge/config.yaml

# Crash Recovery and Graceful Restart Policies
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

# Route stdout and stderr directly to the system journal manager
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: 2. Service Control and Administration Commands
docs.text:
Once the configuration is in place, execute the following commands in sequence to reload the Systemd manager daemon and activate the engine:

# Reload the system daemon configuration profiles
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# Enable TriggerForge to start automatically on system boot
sudo systemctl enable triggerforge.service

# Launch the TriggerForge service immediately
sudo systemctl start triggerforge.service

# Inspect the real-time runtime status and diagnostic brief of the daemon
sudo systemctl status triggerforge.service

docs.title: II. Log Aggregation and System Observability
docs.text: Because TriggerForge delegates its StandardOutput and StandardError completely to journald, operations teams do not need to configure cumbersome log rotation layers (logrotate) at the application level. You can utilize native journalctl commands for efficient, zero-consultation troubleshooting.

docs.title: 1. Real-Time Log Tailing
docs.text:
Run the following command to track the master dispatching sequence, thread pool allocations, and subprocess sandbox stdout in real time:

journalctl -u triggerforge.service -f -n 100

docs.title: 2. Failure Snapshot Diagnostics
docs.text:
When a third-party plugin hits a timeout wall, returns a failed status, or encounters an unhandled segmentation fault (Segfault), the Clerk module writes a structured panic_{plugin_name}_{timestamp}.json report into log_dir (default logs/). It contains target file metadata, the failing plugin and strategy params, environment context, and the full captured stdout / stderr. Use the following commands to pinpoint failures quickly:

# Inspect recent error-level logs (includes panic report paths)
journalctl -u triggerforge.service --priority=err -n 50

# Open the most recent panic report
ls -t logs/panic_*.json | head -1 | xargs -r cat

docs.title: III. 🐳 Cloud-Native Dockerization and Orchestration (v1.2 Preview)
docs.text: To meet agile deployment requirements within cloud-native environments and Kubernetes (K8s) clusters, TriggerForge offers an ultra-lightweight multi-stage build setup integrated with an explicit health checking mechanism.

docs.title: 1. Production-Grade Dockerfile Specification
docs.text:
Create a Dockerfile in the root directory of the project:

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 1: Dependency Assembly and Wheel Packaging (Hatch Backend)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
FROM python:3.11-slim AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Install the modern Hatch packaging frontend
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir hatch

# Copy project declarations and manifest definitions
COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src/ ./src/

# Compile the project into standard distribution wheels
RUN hatch build -t wheel

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 2: Minimal Production Runtime (Kept ultra-pure and lean)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /opt/triggerforge

# Copy compiled wheels from the build stage and execute zero-cache local installations
COPY --from=builder /app/dist/*.whl .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir *.whl \
    && rm *.whl \
    && mkdir -p /opt/triggerforge/storage

# Declare a standard persistent volume mount for target directories
VOLUME ["/opt/triggerforge/storage"]

# Inject standard Python package lookup boundaries
ENV PYTHONPATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages

# Implement the technical health check probe to prevent silent sandbox deadlocks
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD ps aux | grep -v grep | grep triggerforge || exit 1

# Setup a unified system entrypoint
ENTRYPOINT ["triggerforge"]
CMD ["--config", "/opt/triggerforge/storage/config.yaml"]

docs.title: 2. Local Image Compilation and Run Sequences
docs.text:
# Build the production-ready TriggerForge container image
docker build -t triggerforge:v1.1-pro .

# Mount local storage paths and spin up the container in daemonized detached mode
docker run -d \
  --name triggerforge-engine \
  -v /absolute/path/to/local/storage:/opt/triggerforge/storage \
  triggerforge:v1.1-pro

# TriggerForge v1.2 Migration Guide

> **Version**: v1.2-Final (Approved)
> **Status**: Active
> **Path**: docs/en/migration_v1.2.md

## 1. Overview
This guide assists in migrating configurations to the v1.2 standard. Version 1.2 introduces stricter timeout constraints and automated configuration auditing.

## 2. Deprecation & Migration Mapping Table

| Deprecated Key | Recommended Replacement | Disposal Plan | Planned Removal |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `timeout` (Global) | `max_execution_timeout` | Rename (Global hard limit) | v1.4 |
| `strategies[].timeout` | `strategies[].strategy.timeout` | Move to strategy object | v1.4 |
| `debounce_seconds` | (Removed) | Refactored in v1.1 | v1.3 |
| `recursive` | (Removed) | Enabled by default | v1.3 |

## 3. Core Migration Steps

### Step 1: Update Global Configuration
Rename legacy global `timeout` to `max_execution_timeout`.

### Step 2: Adapt Plugin Strategies
Update individual plugin strategies to the new nested schema.

**v1.2 Standard Example:**
```yaml
watch_folders:
  - path: "./data"
    strategies:
      - plugin_name: "OCRProcessor"
        strategy:
          timeout: 60
          priority: "standard"
          allow_override_timeout: false

docs.title: Step 3: Run Configuration Audit
docs.text:
Run the following to verify compliance:

hatch run python scripts/config_manager.py --check

If the return code is 0, the migration is successful.

docs.title: 4. FAQ
docs.text:
Q: How do I verify migration success? A: Run the --check command; a return code of 0 confirms compliance. Results are logged in the audit trail.

Q: Can I mix legacy and new configurations? A: Backward compatibility is supported with DeprecationWarning logs. Complete full migration before v1.4 to avoid potential startup failures.

Q: Why was the priority field introduced? A: To implement resource anti-lockout mechanisms, ensuring high-priority core tasks remain stable.

Technical support and development details are available in Development Plan.

docs.title: 🔌 TriggerForge Plugin Development Specification
docs.text: Version: v1.1-PRO Status: Approved Implementation: src/triggerforge/core/runner/plugin_runner.py Scope: Definitive lifecycle interface guide for internal developers and open-source contributors building modular workflows.

docs.title: I. Architectural Philosophy & Sandbox Constraints
docs.text:
To maintain absolute core resilience, TriggerForge enforces a strict Zero-Trust Plugin Model. Every plugin registered in the execution pipeline is subject to the following runtime guardrails:

  1. Subprocess Sandboxing: Plugins never execute inside the primary monitoring process. They are invoked as independent subprocesses, so memory limits and fatal runtime errors (e.g. segfaults) are safely contained.
  2. Defensive Timeouts: Every plugin lifecycle is bound by a hard execution fence. A plugin blocking beyond its timeout is forcefully terminated and the file is quarantined.
  3. Dynamic Virtual Environments: plugins may target a specific Python runtime via python_path, letting legacy scripts with old dependencies coexist with modern pipelines.
  4. Short-Circuit: strategies for a directory run sequentially; the first failure skips all remaining strategies.

docs.title: II. Plugin Layout & Entrypoint Convention
docs.text:
Plugins are stored in a flat directory layout, one directory per plugin:

{plugin_directory}/           # configured via plugin_directory, default ./plugins
└── my_plugin/                # directory name must equal plugin_name in the strategy
    └── main.py               # entrypoint (alternatives: plugin.py, index.py)

The engine resolves the entrypoint in the order main.py → plugin.py → index.py; if none exists the strategy is considered failed.

docs.title: III. Execution Contract (Process-Level Interface)
docs.text:
Plugins are not wired in via class inheritance. The engine launches your plugin as an executable Python script with this command line:

{interpreter} {plugin_main.py} {target_file} ["{json_params}"]

docs.title: 1. Input Channels
docs.text: Channel Content Notes sys.argv[1] Absolute path of the target file Always provided; the file dropped into the watched directory. sys.argv[2] JSON string of the strategy params Only passed when params is non-empty. Env var TRIGGERFORGE_PARAMS JSON string of the strategy params Only set when params is non-empty; convenient for plugins that do not parse argv. Working directory The engine's current working directory Never assume cwd is the watched directory; use the absolute path from argv[1].

docs.title: 2. Output Contract
docs.text:
A plugin must write exactly one JSON object to stdout describing the outcome:

{"status": "success", "message": "processed 42 rows"}
Field Type Required Description status str Yes "success" means success; any other value is treated as failure. other fields any No Preserved verbatim in the engine result for auditing/logging (e.g. message, rows).

⚠️ Important: any extra stdout output that is not part of the JSON object makes parsing fail and the plugin is marked failed. Send debug output to stderr — the engine records it in the .panic.json diagnostic report.

docs.title: 3. Exit Codes & Failure Semantics
docs.text:
Scenario Engine behavior Exit 0, stdout is valid JSON, status == "success" Success; continue with the next strategy. All success → archive to success_path Non-zero exit code Failure; stderr is captured as the error summary Exit 0 but stdout is not valid JSON Failure ("plugin did not output valid JSON") Runtime exceeds timeout seconds Subprocess killed; failure Uncaught exception Process exits non-zero; failure

On the first failure the engine will: 1. write panic_{plugin_name}_{timestamp}.json into log_dir (default logs/); 2. move the source file into the watch folder's configured error_path.

docs.title: 1. Minimal Plugin
docs.text:
# plugins/my_plugin/main.py
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

def main() -> int:
    target = Path(sys.argv[1])

    # Optional: read strategy params
    params = json.loads(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else {}

    # Your processing logic (example: count bytes)
    size = target.stat().st_size

    # Must emit a single JSON object on stdout
    print(json.dumps({
        "status": "success",
        "file": target.name,
        "size_bytes": size,
        "mode": params.get("mode", "default"),
    }))
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

docs.title: 2. Matching Strategy Configuration
docs.text:
plugin_directory: "./plugins"

watch_folders:
  - path: "./storage/watch_folder"
    success_path: "./storage/success_folder"
    error_path: "./storage/error_folder"
    concurrency: 2
    debounce_seconds: 1.0
    strategies:
      - plugin_name: "my_plugin"     # maps to plugins/my_plugin/main.py
        plugin_version: "1.0.0"
        timeout: 15
        params:
          mode: "strict"

docs.title: 3. Failure Reporting Example
docs.text:
import json
import sys

def main() -> int:
    try:
        # ... business logic ...
        raise ValueError("malformed input")
    except Exception as exc:
        # Failures must also emit JSON so the engine can record a summary
        print(json.dumps({"status": "failed", "error": str(exc)}))
        print(f"traceback details: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)   # details go to stderr
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

docs.title: V. Defensive Coding Guidelines
docs.text:
• Use standard streams only: do not build custom logging backends inside the plugin. The engine captures stdout/stderr from the child process and forwards them to the Clerk layer.
  • Idempotency matters: in high-throughput directory routing a file event may fire more than once. Make processing safe to repeat on the same file.
  • Anchor exceptions: wrap inner logic in try/except. Report failures as a JSON object with a non-success status (and a non-zero exit code) so the file is quarantined instead of silently lost.
  • Never mutate the source path: read from argv[1]; the engine owns archiving (moving the file into the success/error zone).

docs.title: VI. Plugin Self-Test Checklist
docs.text:
Before wiring a plugin into the pipeline, verify it manually in its directory:

# 1. Invoke it exactly as the engine would
python main.py /absolute/path/to/sample.txt '{"mode": "strict"}'

# 2. Confirm stdout is a single valid JSON object with status == "success"
# 3. Confirm the exit code is 0 (bash: echo $? / PowerShell: $LASTEXITCODE)

If the plugin needs its own dependency set, point python_path in the strategy at that virtualenv's interpreter. When the path is invalid the engine logs a warning and falls back to the current interpreter.

docs.title: 🚀 TriggerForge Development Setup Guide
docs.text: Version: v1.1-PRO Status: Approved Scope: Guide for internal developers and open-source contributors on local environment initialization, dependency management, and engineering readiness.

docs.title: I. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before setting up your local environment, ensure your development machine has the following infrastructure installed and configured:

  • Python Runtime: Python 3.11 or newer is required (matching requires-python = ">=3.11" in pyproject.toml).
  • Build System (Hatch, optional): TriggerForge abandons traditional setup.py scripts and fully embraces the PEP 621 standard, using Hatch as its modern packaging and environment management backend. Hatch is optional — plain pip works for all development tasks (see Option B below).
  • Operating System: Fully compatible with Linux (recommended for production), macOS, and Windows.

docs.title: II. Rapid Local Environment Initialization
docs.text: Pick one of the two options below. Either way, install the dependencies before running the tests, otherwise pytest fails during collection with a batch of ModuleNotFoundErrors (import errors, not test failures).

docs.title: Option A: Hatch-Managed Environment (Recommended)
docs.text: All project dependencies, build metadata, and virtual environment management configurations are declared inside pyproject.toml in the project root.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository and Enter the Project Root
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/zybcode/TriggerForge.git
cd TriggerForge

docs.title: 2. Install Hatch (If Not Already Installed)
docs.text:
Hatch serves as both a build utility and an exceptional virtual environment manager. You can install it globally via pip or your system's package manager:

pip install --user hatch

docs.title: 3. Synchronize Environment and Install Dependencies
docs.text:
Run the following command to let Hatch automatically spin up an isolated virtual environment and install the package along with all development and testing dependencies in Editable Mode:

# Initialize the default development environment and install dependencies
hatch env create

docs.title: Option B: Minimal pip Environment
docs.text:
No Hatch required — install the project and test tools into your current interpreter (global or virtualenv) directly:

# 1. Install the project in editable mode (pulls in watchdog / pydantic / pyyaml)
python -m pip install -e .

# 2. Install the test tooling
python -m pip install pytest pytest-cov

# 3. Run the suite from the project root
python -m pytest

💡 Common pitfall: if the interpreter behind your pytest command differs from the one where the dependencies were installed (e.g. pytest.exe lives in Python 3.12's Scripts/ while the deps landed in another Python), you get mass ModuleNotFoundErrors during collection. Verify with pytest --version and where pytest / where python that both sides point to the same environment.

docs.title: 1. Executing the Test Suite
docs.text:
# Option A (Hatch): run pytest with coverage inside the managed environment
hatch run cov

# Option B (pip): run directly from the project root
python -m pytest

# Unit tests only / integration tests only
python -m pytest tests/unit
python -m pytest tests/integration

The current suite contains 47 tests (38 unit + 9 integration) and completes in roughly 10–25 seconds.

docs.title: 2. Running Arbitrary Commands Within the Virtual Environment
docs.text:
If you need to run local diagnostic scripts or tools within the context of your project's virtual environment, use hatch run:

# Inspect the Python version within the virtual environment
hatch run python --version

# Validate your configuration profile against the Pydantic schema (no watchers started)
hatch run triggerforge --config config.yaml --dry-run

docs.title: 3. Entering the Environment Shell
docs.text:
If you prefer to work inside an active virtual environment shell for frequent debugging sessions, launch the managed shell:

hatch shell

Once inside, you can run commands like pytest, python, or triggerforge directly. Simply type exit to safely close the session when finished.

docs.title: IV. Project Directory Layout & Key Paths
docs.text:
Before developing and committing code, make sure you are familiar with our standard src/ layout structure:

TriggerForge/
├── pyproject.toml           # Unified project config file complying with PEP 621 specifications
├── config.yaml              # Runtime config (watched folders & plugin strategies)
├── config.sample.yaml       # Production-grade configuration sample
├── mkdocs.yml               # Docs site navigation config
├── README.md                # Open-source landing page & quick start
├── LICENSE                  # Open-source GNU GPL v3 license text
├── docs/                    # Bilingual documentation site (mkdocs-material)
├── src/                     # Clean source code repository
│   └── triggerforge/
│       ├── main.py          # Engine daemon startup entry point
│       ├── cli.py           # CLI entrypoint (--config / --dry-run / --version)
│       ├── core/
│       │   ├── looper.py    # Orchestrator: queue + worker threads + pipeline wiring
│       │   ├── schema.py    # Pydantic config schemas (single source of truth)
│       │   ├── runner/      # ForgeCore: PluginRunner subprocess sandbox
│       │   ├── sentry/      # Sentry: watcher / queue / filter
│       │   └── clerk/       # Clerk: archiver (file zones) / journal (panic reports)
│       └── plugins/
│           └── base.py      # Optional plugin abstract base class (see plugin_dev.md)
└── tests/
    ├── conftest.py          # Shared fixtures & src path injection
    ├── unit/                # 38 unit tests
    └── integration/         # 9 integration tests (incl. real-watchdog e2e)

⚖️ Important: To prevent dependency conflicts within sandboxed child processes, always declare dependencies in the [project.dependencies] or [tool.hatch.envs.default] blocks of pyproject.toml and sync from there. For everyday local development, Option B's pip install -e . is also a supported path; the key requirement is that the interpreter running pytest is the same one where the dependencies are installed.

docs.title: 欢迎使用 TriggerForge
docs.text: TriggerForge 是一个事件驱动的目录编排引擎：监控文件夹、按配置的插件流水线处理投递进来的文件，并把结果自动归档或隔离。

docs.title: 1. 安装
docs.text: python -m pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. 准备配置
docs.text:
创建 config.yaml（完整字段见 配置参考）：

plugin_directory: "./plugins"

watch_folders:
  - path: "./storage/watch_folder"       # 投递文件到该目录即触发流水线
    success_path: "./storage/success_folder"
    error_path: "./storage/error_folder"
    concurrency: 2
    debounce_seconds: 1.0
    strategies:
      - plugin_name: "my_plugin"         # 对应 plugins/my_plugin/main.py
        timeout: 15
        params:
          mode: "default"

docs.title: 3. 校验并启动
docs.text:
# 仅校验配置，不启动监听
python -m triggerforge.cli --config config.yaml --dry-run

# 启动守护进程
python -m triggerforge.cli --config config.yaml

终端出现 TriggerForge looper is ready to receive files. 后，说明监听器与工作线程均已就绪。

docs.title: 4. 投递文件验证
docs.text:
把任意文件复制到 storage/watch_folder/，引擎会自动：

  1. 等待文件写入完成（防抖窗口）；
  2. 以独立子进程依次执行 strategies 中的插件；
  3. 成功 → 移动到 storage/success_folder/；失败 → 移动到 storage/error_folder/，并在 logs/ 下生成 panic_*.json 诊断报告。

若文件未被处理，请先确认：监控目录路径是否正确、插件入口 plugins/{plugin_name}/main.py 是否存在、以及日志中是否出现 Plugin not found 或 JSON 解析失败提示。

docs.title: 📐 TriggerForge 架构设计文档 (Architecture Specification)
docs.text: 版本：v1.1-PRO 状态：已全量验收 (Approved) 定位：系统核心骨架与隔离模型规范，用于指导模块开发与核心代码实现。

docs.title: 二、 核心分层设计架构
1. Looper (主循环层)
docs.text:
• 核心职责：作为系统的最外层常驻守护进程，负责整个 TriggerForge 引擎的生命周期管理（启动、配置加载、优雅停机与全局信号捕获）。
  • 编排职责：为每个监控目录实例化 SentryWatcher 与 EventBufferQueue，并按 concurrency 启动独立的工作线程消费队列，驱动“插件执行 → 归档”的完整流水线。
  • 自愈机制：在捕获到未知的全局异常时，保障配置不丢失，并具备动态重启下层服务的能力。

docs.title: 2. Sentry (监控哨兵层)
docs.text:
• 核心职责：文件系统事件监听、静态过滤与写入防抖。
  • 技术实现：
  • Watchdog 监听器：对配置的监控目录进行实时文件事件扫描（on_created / on_modified）。
  • 静态过滤：丢弃 .tmp、.swp、~ 结尾及以 . 开头的临时文件，避免编辑器缓存误触发。
  • 写入防抖（Debounce）：为每个文件路径维护独立 Timer，在 debounce_seconds 窗口内重复事件会被取消并重新计时，确保下游读到的是已完整写入的文件。
  • 缓冲投递：防抖窗口结束后，文件路径被投递进线程安全的 EventBufferQueue，实现监听端与执行端的解耦和削峰。

docs.title: 3. ForgeCore (执行中心层)
docs.text:
• 核心职责：插件的宿主环境与核心执行引擎。
  • 执行流程：工作线程从 EventBufferQueue 取出文件路径后，按配置顺序串行执行 strategies；任一策略失败立即短路，跳过后续策略。
  • 沙盒隔离机制（Sandbox Isolation）：
  • 多进程硬隔离：ForgeCore 严禁在主进程或工作线程内直接执行插件代码。对于每一个策略，ForgeCore 会通过 PluginRunner 拉起一个独立的子进程，并以 main.py <文件路径> <JSON参数> 的方式调用。
  • 资源与崩溃防御：插件子进程拥有独立的内存空间与硬性超时熔断机制。若第三方插件发生内存泄漏、陷入死循环或突发崩溃（如段错误 Segfault），受损的仅为该子进程，ForgeCore 会在超时或崩溃后安全回收资源，核心引擎主干保持 100% 炸不烂。
  • 多版本与虚拟环境支持：支持在配置中显式指定 python_path，允许子进程动态调用完全隔离的外部虚拟环境（Venv），解决 legacy 插件与现代依赖的冲突问题；路径无效时自动回退到当前解释器。

docs.title: 4. Clerk (输出管家层)
docs.text:
• 核心职责：负责插件执行完毕后的收尾工作与状态物化。
  • 资产管理：
  • 流水归档：根据子进程返回的执行状态，自动将处理后的文件移动至 success_path（成功归档）或 error_path（失败归档），支持目录自愈创建与同名文件时间戳避让。
  • 诊断报告 (Panic Dump)：当插件失败、超时或崩溃时，Clerk 会生成结构化的 panic_{plugin}_{timestamp}.json，内含目标文件元数据、失败插件与策略参数、环境上下文，以及子进程的 stdout / stderr 全文，为 SRE 和运维团队提供零咨询排查证据。

docs.title: 三、 防御性工程设计规范
1. 架构即代码 (Architecture as Code)
docs.text:
静态文档极易随着代码迭代而失效。TriggerForge 将所有系统配置（如 watch_folders、concurrency、strategies 等）的元数据在 src/triggerforge/core/schema.py 中通过 Python 类型系统 + Pydantic Schema 进行自描述声明，schema.py 是配置字段的唯一定义处。

配套的 docs/zh/configuration.md 与 docs/en/configuration.md 必须与 Schema 保持同步：新增或修改字段后，请同步更新文档中的字段表格；仓库同时提供 tests/unit/test_schema.py::test_repo_sample_config_is_valid 守卫测试，确保 config.yaml 与 config.sample.yaml 始终能通过 Schema 校验，防止配置与实现漂移。

docs.title: 2. 现代 Python 源码布局 (Src Layout)
docs.text: 项目摒弃传统的嵌套包结构，严格采用 src/ 布局（配合 pyproject.toml 的 Hatch 构建后端）。代码主干位于 src/triggerforge/，有效防止本地调试时因嵌套路径污染 PYTHONPATH 而导致的导入隐式报错，确保打包为 Wheel 文件时路径绝对纯净。

docs.title: 3. CI/CD 确定性消除 Flaky Tests
docs.text: 为了确保在 GitHub Actions 等容器化或虚拟化 CI/CD 环境中管道的 100% 稳定，测试目录（tests/）下的集成测试严禁依赖操作系统的真实磁盘 I/O 事件监听。测试套件通过 tests/conftest.py 引入内存队列模拟文件系统（Mock Filesystem）。通过内存事件桩对系统事件进行确定性触发，彻底消除因操作系统事件延迟导致的“偶发性超时测试失败”。

docs.title: 📜 TriggerForge 项目章程 (Project Charter)
docs.text: 版本：v1.1-PRO 状态：已全量验收 (Approved) 定位：明确 TriggerForge 的核心业务痛点、系统边界与技术愿景，作为项目启动的基石文档。

docs.title: 一、 核心业务痛点与项目背景
docs.text:
在现有的企业自动化流水线和数据处理场景中，通过监听目录文件事件来触发后续业务逻辑（如文件解压、格式转换、数据解析等）是非常普遍的需求。然而，现有的常规脚本和轻量工具在生产环境中面临三大致命痛点：

  1. “僵尸文档”与配置漂移：传统的系统配置与开发文档割裂，随着项目快速迭代，文档极易失效，最终变成误导新人的过期垃圾。
  2. “一炸全炸”的插件环境：第三方插件或遗留（Legacy）脚本通常编写质量参差不齐。当插件发生内存泄漏、陷入死循环或突发段错误（Segfault）崩溃时，往往会直接拖垮整个监控主进程，缺乏有效的故障隔离手段。
  3. Flaky Tests（不稳定测试）对 CI/CD 的污染：由于 Watchdog 等底层库依赖操作系统的文件系统事件监听，在 GitHub Actions 等容器化或虚拟化 CI/CD 环境中，经常因磁盘 I/O 延迟表现出极其不稳定的“偶发性超时失败”，极大地消耗了团队的维护精力。

TriggerForge 正是为了彻底终结这些乱象而生。它从设计之初就拒绝做一个“能跑就行”的临时脚本，而是演进为一个具备企业级隔离能力、自动化文档生成、开箱即用部署方案的全生命周期工程产品。

docs.title: 二、 技术愿景与核心目标
docs.text: TriggerForge 的核心愿景是打造一个“跑得稳、炸不烂、文档全、能协作、可开源”的现代事件驱动型目录编排引擎。

docs.title: 1. 核心工程目标
docs.text:
• 架构即代码（Architecture as Code）：利用 Python 类型系统与 Pydantic Schema 作为“活文档”的源头。严禁手动修改配置说明，所有字段元数据由系统配置 Schema 自动生成，消除文档漂移。
  • 多进程硬核沙盒隔离（Sandbox Isolation）：为每个插件的执行拉起独立的子进程，并施加严格的硬性超时熔断机制与资源边界，将故障风险完美锁死在子进程内部。
  • 云原生与 CI/CD 确定性：引入内存队列模拟文件系统的 Mock 机制，绕过容器环境下的真实磁盘 I/O，确保测试管道 100% 稳定通过。

docs.title: 三、 系统边界与功能交付范围 (v1.1-PRO)
1. 准予交付的核心功能 (In Scope)
docs.text:
• 现代化源码布局：采用符合现代 Python 社区最佳实践的标准 src/ 布局与 pyproject.toml 构建配置（基于 Hatch 后端与 PEP 621 标准）。
  • 非阻塞并发事件分发：主循环（Looper）与监听哨兵（Sentry）协作，通过线程安全缓冲队列（EventBufferQueue）与按 concurrency 配置的工作线程池解耦监听与执行，绝不阻塞主监控流。
  • 动态多虚拟环境支持：支持在配置中显式指定 python_path，允许子进程动态调用完全隔离的外部虚拟环境（Venv），完美兼容不同版本的历史插件。
  • 生产级运维闭环：提供开箱即用的 Linux Systemd 服务守护配置与基于 journald 的可观测性日志流追踪，同时在插件故障时自动生成结构化 .panic.json 诊断报告（含 stdout/stderr 全文）进行物化诊断。

docs.title: 2. 明确排除的功能边界 (Out of Scope)
docs.text: • 网络 API 接口：v1.1-PRO 版本定位为纯粹的常驻本地守护进程，不适用且不提供任何基于 HTTP/RESTful 的网络接口，保持极简与纯粹。

docs.title: 四、 商业与开源路线声明
docs.text:
为了平衡社区开源协作的生态红利与企业级闭环的商业价值，TriggerForge 采用双重许可模式（Dual-licensing）：

  1. 开源免费版 (GPL v3)：针对个人学习、学术研究及开源社区使用，代码全面开源，受 GPL 协议的“传染性”保护，任何将其集成的分发产品必须同步开源。
  2. 商业授权版 (Commercial License)：面向希望将 TriggerForge 集成进闭源商业软件或 SaaS 平台的企业客户，提供免除 GPL 传染限制的独立商业许可、高阶插件定制及 SRE 级服务支持。
  3. 贡献者合规性：所有向本项目提交 Pull Request 的外部开发者，必须签署贡献者许可协议（CLA），以保障项目版权的完整性与双重许可的合法分发。

docs.title: ⚙️ TriggerForge 配置指南 (Configuration Specification)
docs.text: 版本：v1.1-PRO 对应代码：src/triggerforge/core/schema.py 说明：本文档中的字段定义与 schema.py 中的 Pydantic 模型保持一致。修改 Schema 后请同步更新本页表格。

docs.title: 一、 全局配置参数
docs.text: TriggerForge 主配置文件采用标准 YAML 格式，核心配置分为全局调度参数与监控目录策略两大模块。

docs.title: 1. 核心字段定义
docs.text: 字段名 类型 默认值 状态 说明 watch_folders List[WatchFolderSchema] 无 (必填) 系统监听的监控目录策略列表，支持配置多个独立目录。 plugin_directory str "./plugins" 可选 插件根目录。引擎在该目录下按 {plugin_name}/main.py 查找插件入口。 debounce_seconds float 1.0 可选 全局默认文件写入防抖窗口（秒），必须大于 0。可被每个监控目录单独覆盖。

docs.title: 2. WatchFolderSchema (监控目录配置对象)
docs.text: 字段名 类型 默认值 状态 说明 path str 无 (必填) 引擎实施事件监听的源目标目录。投递文件至该目录即触发插件流水线。 success_path str 无 (必填) 插件流水线全部执行成功后，源文件被原子化移动至该归档目录。 error_path str 无 (必填) 任一插件执行失败或超时熔断后，源文件被移动至该故障隔离目录。 concurrency int 1 可选 该监控目录分配的工作线程数量，必须大于 0。 debounce_seconds float 1.0 可选 该目录专属的写入防抖窗口（秒），必须大于 0。 strategies List[StrategySchema] 无 (必填) 事件触发后按顺序串行执行的插件策略流水线。

docs.title: 3. StrategySchema (插件执行策略配置对象)
docs.text: 字段名 类型 默认值 状态 说明 plugin_name str 无 (必填) 插件目录名，引擎据此定位 {plugin_directory}/{plugin_name}/main.py。 plugin_version str "0.0.0" 可选 插件版本标识，用于运行时校验与审计。 timeout int 30 可选 该插件子进程的硬超时熔断秒数，必须大于 0。超时将被强制终止。 params Dict[str, Any] {} 可选 传递给插件的动态自定义参数，会以 JSON 注入子进程。 python_path Optional[str] None 可选 指定独立解释器（虚拟环境）路径。路径不存在时自动回退到当前解释器。

docs.title: 二、 完整配置示例 (config.sample.yaml)
docs.text:
下面是一个生产就绪的配置示例。你可以直接复制此内容创建你的 config.yaml 并部署到生产环境中：

# =================================================================
# TriggerForge 生产级配置文件示例
# =================================================================

# 插件根目录：引擎在 {plugin_directory}/{plugin_name}/main.py 下查找入口
plugin_directory: "./plugins"

# 全局默认防抖窗口（秒），可被每个监控目录覆盖
debounce_seconds: 1.0

watch_folders:
  - path: "./storage/watch_folder"       # 投递文件到该目录即触发流水线
    success_path: "./storage/success_folder"
    error_path: "./storage/error_folder"
    concurrency: 4                       # 该目录独立的工作线程数量
    debounce_seconds: 1.0                # 该目录专属防抖窗口

    strategies:
      # 策略 1：调用现代压缩插件，限时 15 秒熔断
      - plugin_name: "compress_plugin"
        plugin_version: "1.0.0"
        timeout: 15                      # 15秒硬超时防锁死
        params:
          level: "high"
          archive_type: "tar.gz"

      # 策略 2：调用历史遗留数据解析插件，挂载独立的虚拟环境运行
      - plugin_name: "legacy_parser_plugin"
        plugin_version: "0.8.2"
        # 核心亮点：打破依赖冲突，子进程动态切换至老旧的独立隔离环境运行
        python_path: "/opt/venv/legacy_env/bin/python"
        timeout: 30                      # 30秒超时熔断
        params:
          legacy_mode: true
          encoding: "gbk"

docs.title: 三、 运行时行为说明
docs.text:
1. 事件链路：文件写入监控目录 → 防抖窗口等待写入完成 → 进入事件缓冲队列 → 工作线程消费 → 串行执行 strategies。
  2. 短路熔断：strategies 中任一策略执行失败，后续策略不再执行，直接进入失败归档。
  3. 归档策略：全部策略成功 → success_path；任一失败 → 生成 .panic.json 诊断报告并移动至 error_path。
  4. 配置校验：启动时通过 TriggerForgeConfigSchema 校验；使用 --dry-run 可在不启动监听的情况下仅做校验。

docs.title: 简体中文
docs.text:
# ⚙️ TriggerForge 生产环境部署与运维手册 (Deployment & Operations Guide)

> **版本**：v1.1-PRO  
> **状态**：已全量验收 (Approved)  
> **定位**：面向 SRE、运维团队与系统管理员的生产级常驻守护进程部署与容器化编排指南。

---

## 一、 使用 Systemd 进行进程守护 (Linux 推荐)

TriggerForge 作为常驻型事件驱动引擎，在 Linux 生产环境中必须通过 Systemd 进程守护管理器进行配置，以保障系统的开机自启与崩溃自愈能力。

### 1. 创建服务配置文件
请在 `/etc/systemd/system/triggerforge.service` 路径下创建服务守护文件，并写入以下配置：

```ini
[Unit]
Description=TriggerForge Event-Driven Directory Orchestration Engine
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=triggerforge
Group=triggerforge
WorkingDirectory=/opt/triggerforge

# 核心细节：注入正确的全局 PYTHONPATH 以适配现代 src/ 布局结构
Environment=PYTHONPATH=/opt/triggerforge/src

# 调用虚拟环境中的 Python 解释器直接拉起核心 main 模块
ExecStart=/opt/triggerforge/venv/bin/python -m triggerforge.main --config /opt/triggerforge/config.yaml

# 崩溃自愈与优雅重启策略
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

# 日志直接导向系统的标准日志管理器 journald
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: 2. 服务控制与管理指令
docs.text:
配置完成后，依次执行以下命令刷新 Systemd 守护进程并启动服务：

# 重新加载系统守护进程配置
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# 启用 TriggerForge 开机自启
sudo systemctl enable triggerforge.service

# 启动 TriggerForge 服务
sudo systemctl start triggerforge.service

# 查看服务当前的实时运行状态与诊断简报
sudo systemctl status triggerforge.service

docs.title: 二、 日志流收集与系统观测
docs.text: 由于 TriggerForge 的 StandardOutput 和 StandardError 已完全托管给 journald，运维团队无需在应用层配置繁琐的日志轮转（Logrotate），直接使用 journalctl 即可实现零咨询的高效运维观测。

docs.title: 1. 实时日志滚动追踪
docs.text:
使用以下命令实时追踪主进程的调度流水、线程池状态以及沙盒进程的输出流：

journalctl -u triggerforge.service -f -n 100

docs.title: 2. 诊断与排查故障快照
docs.text:
当第三方插件触发超时熔断、返回失败状态或未捕获的段错误（Segfault）时，Clerk 模块会在 log_dir（默认 logs/）下生成结构化的 panic_{plugin_name}_{timestamp}.json 诊断报告，内含目标文件元数据、失败插件与策略参数、环境上下文以及子进程的 stdout / stderr 全文。可以配合以下指令快速定向排查：

# 查看近期错误级日志（含 panic 报告落盘路径）
journalctl -u triggerforge.service --priority=err -n 50

# 列出并查看最近一份故障现场报告
ls -t logs/panic_*.json | head -1 | xargs -r cat

docs.title: 三、 🐳 Docker 容器化编排部署 (v1.2 预告版)
docs.text: 为了满足云原生及 Kubernetes (K8s) 环境下的敏捷部署需求，TriggerForge 提供了超轻量的多阶段构建（Multi-stage Build）方案，并集成了硬性守护进程健康检查探针。

docs.title: 1. 生产级 Dockerfile 镜像定义
docs.text:
在项目根目录下创建 Dockerfile：

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 阶段 1：依赖构建与 Wheel 打包 (使用现代 Hatch 后端)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
FROM python:3.11-slim AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# 安装 Hatch 构建工具
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir hatch

# 复制项目骨架与构建定义
COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src/ ./src/

# 构建标准发布 Wheel 包
RUN hatch build -t wheel

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 阶段 2：生产常驻运行镜像 (保持绝对纯净与轻量)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /opt/triggerforge

# 从构建阶段复制打包好的包并直接进行无缓存本地安装
COPY --from=builder /app/dist/*.whl .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir *.whl \
    && rm *.whl \
    && mkdir -p /opt/triggerforge/storage

# 显式声明持久化挂载卷，供外部被监听目录接入
VOLUME ["/opt/triggerforge/storage"]

# 注入 Python 运行时标准包查找路径
ENV PYTHONPATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages

# 引入终审技术强化的容器健康检查 (Healthcheck) 探针，防范沙盒僵死
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD ps aux | grep -v grep | grep triggerforge || exit 1

# 设置容器统一入口点
ENTRYPOINT ["triggerforge"]
CMD ["--config", "/opt/triggerforge/storage/config.yaml"]

docs.title: 2. 本地镜像构建与试运行指令
docs.text:
# 编译生成 TriggerForge 容器镜像
docker build -t triggerforge:v1.1-pro .

# 挂载本地存储目录并以后台常驻模式拉起容器
docker run -d \
  --name triggerforge-engine \
  -v /absolute/path/to/local/storage:/opt/triggerforge/storage \
  triggerforge:v1.1-pro

docs.title: Dev plan v1.2
docs.text:
针对评审专家提出的最后 2 项修正要求（补充 priority 约束说明及统一状态标记），以下是最终修正后的完整版 dev_plan_v1.2.md，可直接确认归档。

# TriggerForge v1.2 开发规划文档

> **版本**：v1.2-Final (已修正)
> **状态**：已修正（待归档）
> **目录**：docs/zh/dev_plan_v1.2.md

## 1. 概述
本版本致力于实现 TriggerForge 的运维自动化闭环，核心目标是提升系统在高负载下的稳定性与防锁死能力，并正式引入配置热加载机制，为未来商业化工具链提供稳定的基座支持。

## 2. 核心任务清单
| 序号 | 任务模块 | 关键开发内容 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Schema 扩展** | 实现 `priority` 与 `allow_override_timeout` 校验逻辑及 `metadata` 扩展槽[cite: 9]。 |
| 2 | **配置审计引擎** | 开发 `ForgeConfigManager`，支持 `--check` 模式与结构化 JSON 输出[cite: 9]。 |
| 3 | **热加载机制** | 实现 `SIGHUP` 信号监听，支持原子化配置切换与回滚降级[cite: 9]。 |
| 4 | **迁移指引** | 编写 `migration_v1.2.md`，明确弃用状态及迁移路径[cite: 9]。 |
| 5 | **集成测试** | 覆盖豁免越权、热加载一致性及原子切换测试[cite: 9]。 |

## 3. 技术详细实现要求

### 3.1 双重约束校验逻辑 (`src/triggerforge/core/schema.py`)
在 `PluginStrategySchema` 模型中实现 `model_validator`[cite: 9]：
* **强制约束**: 当 `allow_override_timeout = true` 时，必须同时指定 `priority = "high"`。若条件不满足，引擎在启动预检阶段抛出 `ValueError` 并拒绝启动，确保系统安全性[cite: 9]。
* **商业扩展预留**: 新增 `metadata` 字典字段，用于承载未来商业版本需要的数字签名、License Hash 或客户授权信息。该设计保持了 YAML 结构的向前兼容性[cite: 9]。

### 3.2 配置审计接口与热加载处理 (`src/triggerforge/utils/config_manager.py`)
* **热加载原子性校验**: 接收 `SIGHUP` 后，触发 `ForgeConfigManager` 进行审计。若新配置校验失败，则**保持当前运行配置不变**，输出错误审计日志并发出告警，确保系统状态不因错误配置而崩溃[cite: 9]。
* **退出码规范**: 0 (合规), 1 (违规), 2 (语法错误), 3 (内部执行异常)[cite: 9]。

### 3.3 热加载机制 (`src/triggerforge/engine/core.py`)
* **原子切换**: 采用“校验-替换”原子操作，非逐字段替换，确保热加载流程中系统内存中的配置集始终保持一致性[cite: 9]。
* **审计追踪**: 切换完成后，系统强制输出审计变更摘要（含前后配置对比），并更新运行状态日志[cite: 9]。

## 4. 插件开发对齐标准
* **标准化输出**: 插件须遵循 JSON 日志规范[cite: 9]。
* **优先级枚举**: 统一枚举值：`high` (高), `standard` (标准), `low` (低)[cite: 9]。
* **约束说明**: **仅当 `priority = "high"` 时，`allow_override_timeout` 字段才能设置为 `true`。`standard` 与 `low` 级别不支持超时覆盖。**

## 5. 测试策略
* **单元测试**: 使用 `hatch run pytest tests/test_config_manager.py -v` 执行配置审计模块专项测试。针对 `SIGHUP` 触发的重载逻辑增加时序测试，确保原子性切换[cite: 9]。
* **集成测试**: 将 `--check` 模式接入 Git Hooks，并增加自动化脚本模拟配置文件变更与信号发送，确保热加载流程稳定性[cite: 9]。

---
*注：本开发规划已符合架构评审要求，待最终归档。参考 [迁移指南](./migration_v1.2.md)。*

docs.title: Migration v1.2
docs.text:
# TriggerForge v1.2 版本迁移指南

> **版本**：v1.2-Final (已修正)
> **状态**：生效中
> **目录**：docs/zh/migration_v1.2.md

## 1. 概述
本指南旨在协助用户将 TriggerForge 的配置文件升级至 v1.2 标准。v1.2 版本引入了更严格的超时约束与配置审计机制，部分旧有的配置项已被弃用，建议尽早完成迁移[cite: 8]。

## 2. 弃用字段与迁移映射表

| 弃用配置项 | 实际状态 | 迁移方案 | 移除版本 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `timeout` (全局) | 弃用 | 映射至 `max_execution_timeout` | v1.4[cite: 8] |
| `strategies[].timeout` | 兼容 | 归纳至 `strategy.timeout` | v1.4[cite: 8] |
| `debounce_seconds` | 已失效 | v1.1 已重构，配置将被忽略 | v1.3[cite: 8] |
| `recursive` | 已失效 | 默认开启，配置将被忽略 | v1.3[cite: 8] |

## 3. 核心迁移步骤

### 第一步：更新全局配置
将旧的 `timeout` 参数重命名为 `max_execution_timeout`，作为系统的安全底线[cite: 8]。

### 第二步：适配插件策略
将原有的插件配置更新至 `strategy` 嵌套对象中[cite: 8]。

**v1.2 标准配置示例：**
```yaml
watch_folders:
  - path: "./data"
    strategies:
      - plugin_name: "OCRProcessor"
        strategy: 
          timeout: 60
          priority: "high"             # 必须为 high 以支持超时覆盖
          allow_override_timeout: true # 需与 priority: high 组合使用

docs.title: 第三步：合规性预检
docs.text:
迁移完成后，运行以下命令验证配置合规性：

hatch run python scripts/config_manager.py --check

如果输出返回值为 0，则迁移成功。

docs.title: 4. 商业扩展兼容承诺
docs.text: 本版本配置结构已预留 metadata 扩展槽，确保现有 v1.2 配置在后续升级商业版（启用数字签名校验）时，无需进行任何格式调整，实现“平滑演进”。

docs.title: 5. 常见问题 (FAQ)
docs.text:
Q：如何验证迁移是否成功？ A：运行上述 --check 命令，若无错误输出且退出码为 0，则表示配置合规。审计结果将自动记录在系统审计日志中。

Q：新旧配置可以混用吗？ A：v1.2 支持向下兼容，但会触发 DeprecationWarning 日志。为了确保 v1.4 版本升级平滑，请务必在近期内完成全量迁移。

Q：为什么新增了优先级字段及 allow_override_timeout？ A：为了实现“资源防锁死”机制。注意：当您设置 allow_override_timeout = true 时，必须同时将 priority 设为 high，否则系统将在启动时抛出配置校验异常，拒绝启动。

Q：商业扩展的元数据字段会影响当前运行吗？ A：不会。metadata 字段在 v1.2 中仅作占位处理，且在启动校验阶段已被设计为忽略，确保开源版本用户无感使用。

技术支持与开发详情可参考 开发规划。

docs.title: 🔌 TriggerForge 插件开发规范 (Plugin Development Specification)
docs.text: 版本: v1.1-PRO 状态: 已批准 对应实现: src/triggerforge/core/runner/plugin_runner.py 适用范围: 为构建模块化工作流的内部开发者及开源社区贡献者提供的权威生命周期接口指南。

docs.title: I. 架构理念与沙箱约束
docs.text:
为了确保核心引擎的绝对鲁棒性，TriggerForge 执行严格的 “零信任插件模型”。在执行流水线中注册的每一个插件都必须遵守以下运行时防护机制：

  1. 子进程沙箱 (Subprocess Sandboxing)：插件绝不会在核心监控进程内执行。它们作为独立的子进程被调用，确保内存限制和致命运行时错误（如段错误 Segfaults）被安全地隔离。
  2. 防御性超时 (Defensive Timeouts)：每个插件的生命周期都受严格的时间围栏限制。如果插件锁定或阻塞超过 timeout 阈值，子进程将被强制终止，文件进入故障隔离区。
  3. 动态虚拟环境 (Dynamic Virtual Environments)：插件可通过 python_path 明确指定特定的 Python 运行时。这使得需要旧版本依赖的遗留脚本能够与现代流水线无缝共存。
  4. 短路熔断 (Short-Circuit)：同一目录的 strategies 串行执行，任一插件失败则后续插件不再执行。

docs.title: II. 插件目录与入口约定
docs.text:
插件以扁平化目录形式存放，一个插件一个目录：

{plugin_directory}/           # 由配置项 plugin_directory 指定，默认 ./plugins
└── my_plugin/                # 目录名必须与策略中的 plugin_name 完全一致
    └── main.py               # 入口文件（备选：plugin.py、index.py）

引擎按 main.py → plugin.py → index.py 的顺序查找入口文件，全部缺失时该策略判定为失败。

docs.title: III. 执行契约（进程级接口）
docs.text:
插件不是通过类继承接入的，而是作为一个可执行的 Python 脚本被引擎拉起。引擎构建的命令行如下：

{interpreter} {plugin_main.py} {target_file} ["{json_params}"]

docs.title: 1. 输入通道
docs.text: 通道 内容 说明 sys.argv[1] 目标文件的绝对路径 必传。即投递到监控目录、触发本次流水的文件。 sys.argv[2] 策略 params 的 JSON 字符串 仅在 params 非空时传入。 环境变量 TRIGGERFORGE_PARAMS 策略 params 的 JSON 字符串 仅在 params 非空时设置，便于不解析 argv 的插件读取。 工作目录 引擎进程的当前工作目录 插件不应假设 cwd 为监控目录，请使用 argv[1] 的绝对路径。

docs.title: 2. 输出契约
docs.text:
插件必须向 stdout 输出且仅输出一个 JSON 对象，用于告知引擎执行结果：

{"status": "success", "message": "processed 42 rows"}
字段 类型 必填 说明 status str 是 值为 "success" 表示成功；其他值均视为失败并转入故障隔离区。 其他字段 任意 否 会原样保留在引擎的返回值中，可用于审计与日志（如 message、rows）。

⚠️ 重要：若插件在 stdout 打印了额外的调试信息（非 JSON），引擎将因 JSON 解析失败判定该插件失败。调试信息请写入 stderr，引擎会把它记录进诊断报告（.panic.json）。

docs.title: 3. 退出码与失败判定
docs.text:
场景 引擎行为 退出码 0 且 stdout 为合法 JSON 且 status == "success" 判定成功，继续执行下一个策略；全部成功则归档至 success_path 退出码非 0 判定失败，捕获 stderr 作为错误摘要 退出码 0 但 stdout 非合法 JSON 判定失败（提示插件未输出合法 JSON） 超过 timeout 秒未退出 强制终止子进程，判定失败 抛出未捕获异常 进程以非零码退出，判定失败

任一策略失败后，引擎会： 1. 在 log_dir（默认 logs/）下生成 panic_{plugin_name}_{timestamp}.json 故障现场诊断报告； 2. 将源文件移动至该监控目录配置的 error_path。

docs.title: 1. 最小可用插件
docs.text:
# plugins/my_plugin/main.py
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

def main() -> int:
    target = Path(sys.argv[1])

    # 可选：读取策略参数
    params = json.loads(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else {}

    # 你的处理逻辑（示例：统计文件字节数）
    size = target.stat().st_size

    # 必须向 stdout 输出单个 JSON 对象
    print(json.dumps({
        "status": "success",
        "file": target.name,
        "size_bytes": size,
        "mode": params.get("mode", "default"),
    }))
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

docs.title: 2. 对应的策略配置
docs.text:
plugin_directory: "./plugins"

watch_folders:
  - path: "./storage/watch_folder"
    success_path: "./storage/success_folder"
    error_path: "./storage/error_folder"
    concurrency: 2
    debounce_seconds: 1.0
    strategies:
      - plugin_name: "my_plugin"     # 对应 plugins/my_plugin/main.py
        plugin_version: "1.0.0"
        timeout: 15
        params:
          mode: "strict"

docs.title: 3. 失败上报示例
docs.text:
import json
import sys

def main() -> int:
    try:
        # ... 业务逻辑 ...
        raise ValueError("malformed input")
    except Exception as exc:
        # 失败也必须输出 JSON，便于引擎记录错误摘要
        print(json.dumps({"status": "failed", "error": str(exc)}))
        print(f"traceback details: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)   # 详细信息走 stderr
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

docs.title: V. 插件自测清单
docs.text:
在接入流水线前，请在插件目录下手动验证：

# 1. 直接用引擎相同的命令行调用插件
python main.py /absolute/path/to/sample.txt '{"mode": "strict"}'

# 2. 确认 stdout 是单个合法 JSON 且 status 为 success
# 3. 确认退出码为 0（Windows: echo %ERRORLEVEL% / bash: echo $?）

若插件需要独立依赖环境，请在策略中配置 python_path 指向该虚拟环境的解释器；路径无效时引擎会告警并回退到当前解释器执行。

docs.title: 🚀 TriggerForge 环境搭建与开发指南 (Development Setup Guide)
docs.text: 版本：v1.1-PRO 状态：已全量验收 (Approved) 定位：面向内部开发人员与开源贡献者的本地开发环境初始化、依赖管理与工程就绪指南。

docs.title: 一、 开发环境前置要求
docs.text:
在开始搭建环境之前，请确保您的开发机已安装并配置好以下基础设施：

  • Python 运行时：需要 Python 3.11 及以上（与 pyproject.toml 中 requires-python = ">=3.11" 保持一致）。
  • 构建系统（Hatch，可选）：TriggerForge 摒弃了传统的 setup.py，全面拥抱 PEP 621 标准，使用 Hatch 作为现代打包与环境管理后端。不使用 Hatch 时，直接用 pip 亦可完成全部开发工作（见下文方案 B）。
  • 操作系统：支持 Linux (推荐用于生产部署)、macOS 以及 Windows。

docs.title: 二、 快速初始化本地开发环境
docs.text: 以下两种方案任选其一。无论哪种方案，都必须先把依赖装齐再跑测试，否则 pytest 会在收集阶段报一批 ModuleNotFoundError（而不是用例失败）。

docs.title: 方案 A：Hatch 托管环境（推荐）
docs.text: 我们已经将所有的依赖、构建元数据以及虚拟环境管理配置写入了根目录下的 pyproject.toml。

docs.title: 1. 克隆项目并进入根目录
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/zybcode/TriggerForge.git
cd TriggerForge

docs.title: 2. 安装 Hatch（如果尚未安装）
docs.text:
Hatch 既是构建工具，也是极佳的虚拟环境管理器。您可以通过 pip 或系统包管理器直接全局安装它：

pip install --user hatch

docs.title: 3. 一键同步环境并安装依赖
docs.text:
运行以下命令，Hatch 会自动为您创建独立的虚拟环境，并以可编辑模式（Editable Mode）安装项目及其所有的开发与测试依赖：

# 激活默认的开发环境并安装所有依赖
hatch env create

docs.title: 方案 B：极简 pip 环境
docs.text:
不需要 Hatch，直接用 pip 把项目和测试工具装进当前解释器（全局或虚拟环境均可）：

# 1. 以可编辑模式安装项目本体（自动带上 watchdog / pydantic / pyyaml 运行依赖）
python -m pip install -e .

# 2. 安装测试工具
python -m pip install pytest pytest-cov

# 3. 从项目根目录运行测试
python -m pytest

💡 常见坑：如果 pytest 命令挂载的解释器与安装依赖的解释器不是同一个（例如 pytest.exe 在 Python 3.12 的 Scripts 下，而依赖装到了别的 Python），就会出现"测试收集阶段大面积 ModuleNotFoundError"。可用 pytest --version、where pytest / where python 核对两边是否为同一环境。

docs.title: 三、 本地日常开发核心指令
1. 运行测试套件
docs.text:
# 方案 A（Hatch）：在独立虚拟环境中自动运行 pytest 并输出覆盖率
hatch run cov

# 方案 B（pip）：从项目根目录直接运行
python -m pytest

# 仅运行单元测试 / 集成测试
python -m pytest tests/unit
python -m pytest tests/integration

当前测试套件共 47 个用例（38 个单元测试 + 9 个集成测试），全绿约需 10~25 秒。

docs.title: 2. 在虚拟环境中执行任意命令
docs.text:
如果您需要直接运行本地的代码脚本或排查工具，可以使用 hatch run：

# 检查当前虚拟环境中的 Python 版本
hatch run python --version

# 验证您的配置文件是否合规（利用 Pydantic Schema 校验，不启动监听）
hatch run triggerforge --config config.yaml --dry-run

docs.title: 3. 手动激活环境 Shell
docs.text:
如果您更喜欢保持激活虚拟环境的状态进行高频调试，可以使用以下命令进入虚拟环境的 Shell：

hatch shell

进入后，您可以直接像平常一样运行 pytest、python 或 triggerforge，调试完毕后输入 exit 即可安全退出。

docs.title: 四、 项目骨架与关键路径说明
docs.text:
在开发和提交代码前，请务必熟悉以下标准的 src/ 布局结构：

TriggerForge/
├── pyproject.toml           # 遵循 PEP 621 规范的统一项目配置文件
├── config.yaml              # 运行配置（监控目录与插件策略）
├── config.sample.yaml       # 生产级配置示例
├── mkdocs.yml               # 文档站点导航配置
├── README.md                # 开源门户与快速开始
├── LICENSE                  # 开源 GPLv3 授权文件
├── docs/                    # 中英双语文档站（mkdocs-material）
├── src/                     # 纯净的源码存放目录
│   └── triggerforge/
│       ├── main.py          # 引擎守护进程启动入口
│       ├── cli.py           # 命令行入口（--config / --dry-run / --version）
│       ├── core/
│       │   ├── looper.py    # 编排层：队列 + 工作线程 + 插件流水线接线
│       │   ├── schema.py    # Pydantic 核心配置 Schema（配置的唯一定义处）
│       │   ├── runner/      # ForgeCore：PluginRunner 子进程沙箱
│       │   ├── sentry/      # Sentry：watcher / queue / filter
│       │   └── clerk/       # Clerk：archiver（归档）/ journal（panic 报告）
│       └── plugins/
│           └── base.py      # 可选的插件抽象基类（进程契约见 plugin_dev.md）
└── tests/
    ├── conftest.py          # 共享 fixture 与 src 路径注入
    ├── unit/                # 38 个单元测试
    └── integration/         # 9 个集成测试（含真实 watchdog 端到端）

⚖️ 注意：为防范沙盒子进程依赖冲突，请始终通过 pyproject.toml 的 [project.dependencies] 或 [tool.hatch.envs.default] 声明依赖，再执行同步。日常本地开发使用上文方案 B 的 pip install -e . 也是受支持的方式；关键是保证运行 pytest 的解释器与安装依赖的解释器一致。
